### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via aiExposed (symbol, a field of interface FlowStartDoor))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via aiExposed (symbol, a field of interface FlowStartDoor))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via flowStartRefusal (symbol, a top-level function), resolveRunDataContext (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via dispatchFlowAction (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 52 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e8b56d4793f74a5317739f57007dcb5af5c71724` — the merge of head `7de0545a6e658b43a49af23c92fe4674a51b0ea7` into base `1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e8b56d4793f74a5317739f57007dcb5af5c71724 && git checkout e8b56d4793f74a5317739f57007dcb5af5c71724
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 7de0545a6e658b43a49af23c92fe4674a51b0ea7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 && git merge --no-ff 7de0545a6e658b43a49af23c92fe4674a51b0ea7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `183ed607592e8bd2fcd31327778c85cc07c30380`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0151-ai-service-account-a-headless-agent-is-a-registered-principal-of-its-own.md, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-start-required-permissions.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-agent-account-kind.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts, .changeset/31874-ai-account-elevated-flow-start.md + (read, not reviewed) packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-slot-view.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/services/service-print/src/print-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-permission-sets.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/system/apis/index.ts, hotcrm src/**/flows/*.flow.ts (at 8277e61f)

Inputs read: card #31874 body and its five comments (ruling 6812617393, claims 6836684353 and 6836939154, report 6838841457), PR #32912 body, file list (11 files) and net diff, check-runs on the head. Check-runs at 2026-11-12T23:28Z: 50 listed, 25 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 9 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · consumer gates). Those nine have no verdict yet; this record does not stand in for them, and the seat reads them before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, trigger routes (`POST /automation/NAME/trigger` and the legacy `trigger/NAME`, both through `respondToFlowTrigger`): an AI service account at a `runAs: 'system'` flow of type `screen` or `api` moves from admitted to `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. Narrowing. Right, and inside the ruling.
- Accept set, declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint (`executeFlow`): the same move. Right.
- Accept set, REST actions route (`dispatchFlowAction`): the account is refused when the `type: 'flow'` action does not declare `ai.exposed: true`, admitted when it does. Narrowing. Right.
- Accept set, MCP `run_action`: unchanged. The exposure gate upstream already refuses an unexposed action for every caller, so rule 2 can only see `aiExposed: true` there. Right.
- Not moved, confirmed in the tree: a person, an OAuth-delegated agent (`onBehalfOf` set), the system principal (`isSystem` returns before any rule), an account at a `runAs: 'user'` or undeclared flow, the resume routes, flows that start on their own trigger. Rule 1 still answers an account first; `requiredPermissions` still answers an admitted account.
- Refusal: `PERMISSION_DENIED` and 403 reach the caller at all three call sites (trigger: `deps.error(message, status, { code })`; endpoint: `apiErrorResponse`; action door: thrown with `status` and `code`, mapped by `isFlowActionRefusal`). No new code is minted. Right.
- Run facts: the system arm of `resolveRunDataContext` now carries `principalKind: 'agent'` when the run context does; `seedRunGrants` keeps the door-forwarded kind on a system run. Additive on an internal envelope. The readers I found either test `isSystem` first (print service) or are reached only after elevation has answered, so nothing is narrowed or widened for the run's own operations. A `runAs: 'user'` hook fired by one of the run's writes now de-elevates to an agent context, which is the narrower and correct answer. The decider switch still deletes the kind before a system run's decision segment. Right.
- Public surface: `flowStartRefusal` gains a required fourth argument and `isAiServiceAccount`, `actionIsAiExposed`, `AI_ACCOUNT_ELEVATED_START_REFUSAL`, `FlowStartDoor` are new exports of their modules. None is re-exported from `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, so no published signature moves. `packages/spec` is untouched: no key, no accept set of any schema. Right.
- `isAiServiceAccount` matches the assembler: `principalKind: 'agent'` with `onBehalfOf` set only for the OAuth agent (`assemble-execution-context.ts` lines 332 to 366). Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/service-automation`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required`, no key or stored row moves). That is what AGENTS.md asks of a non-protocol breaking change, and both packages the diff moves are named. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is present and identical in the PR body and the changeset; the diff widens nothing I could find. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` concluded success on the head. Matches.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions (report 6838841457):
1. By-name doors, A or B. Reviewed from the code. A admits a strict subset of what the ruling's words allow, so it cannot breach the ruling; B would let an opt-in written on one action open two doors that ask none of that action's guards, and needs a lookup the ruling does not spell. The "flow carries the opt-in" half of the ruling has nowhere to be written (Flow and Endpoint declare no `ai` key, and the ruling adds none), so under A only the action half is live. ESCALATED to the maintainer: the ADR sentence in this PR is written for A, so his Tier H approval should be given with that answer; a later B amends that sentence in the same change.
2. `ai.requiresConfirmation` on REST for an account. Answered: A for this PR. The ruling's rule is the opt-in, and the confirmation gate is a separate, standing boundary. One thing the answer leaves open, should-fix S2 below.
3. "What counts as a start door": one item is with the seat.

Dev flags:
- `security_findings: withheld`: one item is with the seat. Nothing of it is judged here.
- Out of scope, `packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts` prose: confirmed at line 98, and it is a published `.describe()` string. See S1.
- Out of scope, three `content/docs` pages: confirmed for `flows.mdx` line 77 (the door sentence has no account row). See S1.
- Out of scope, a self-triggered system run carries no kind: confirmed unchanged, and outside the ruling (it speaks of the run a door admits).
- Deviations: `pnpm lint` run once per head, accepted. Package suites and the service-automation typecheck ran on the head's parent: the head adds one import line to one runtime test file, and Test Core on the head is the verdict (pending, above). `test:repo` left to CI: accepted. No `scripts/adr-anchors` entry: the sentence's `path#symbol` anchor resolves to an exported function, and every Lint check-run on the head concluded success. Claim re-posted with the tier constant in place of a model id: accepted.
- First-party reach, verified: every hotcrm flow declaring `runAs: 'system'` (23 files) is `schedule`, `record_change` or `autolaunched`, already closed by rule 1. In this repo two flows change their answer for an account: `showcase_inquiry_purge` (`screen`, behind `POST /api/v1/apps/showcase/inquiries/purge` and the trigger route; no flow action targets it) and `showcase_inbound_task_webhook` (`api`, trigger route only). The dev's count holds.

### ④ Design judgment

ADR file. One line added, in Non-goals, nothing else in `docs/adr/**`. Against ruling C: "refused by default", "the author's existing `ai.exposed: true` opt-in" and "`principalKind` on its run facts" are each in the sentence. It says "the action that starts it" where the ruling says "the flow (or the action that starts it)", which is reading A stated as the rule (③ item 1). Against its first consumer, `flowStartRefusal`: the sentence describes what the function does at the three call sites, and the anchor resolves. Holds, on reading A.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence against the ruling:
- "Refused by default": rule 2 is one `if` in `flowStartRefusal`, after rule 1 and before `requiredPermissions`, and it refuses unless `door.aiExposed === true` (strict). Agrees.
- "Admitted only with the existing opt-in": the action door hands `actionIsAiExposed(action)` on the resolved declaration, the literal `true` and nothing else; the two by-name doors hand `false`. No door admits more than the ruling. Agrees.
- "One rule on every door": `flowStartRefusal` has exactly three callers, and they are the only three request-reached `execute` calls in `packages/runtime` (action door, trigger routes, declared endpoint); MCP reaches the first. A repo-wide search for other callers of the automation service's `execute` found the engine's own nodes, the verify harness and nothing else that a request reaches. The argument is required, so a fourth door does not compile without stating it. No door missed among the doors; one item is with the seat.
- "No second copy": `ai?.exposed === true` now appears once in `packages/runtime` and `packages/mcp` (the MCP tools read the bridge's attested `aiExposed`). The account reading is one function, used by the rule and by both context builders. Agrees.
- "Refusal by name telling the author which opt-in to add": one frozen constant, same words at every door, names `ai: { exposed: true, description }` on a `type: 'flow'` action and the two doors where it stands, and nothing of the flow. Pinned by code, status and message, with `execute` asserted uncalled. Agrees.
- "No new spec key": `packages/spec` untouched. Agrees.
- "`principalKind` on the system-run branch's run facts": door forward, `seedRunGrants` keep, system arm carry; pinned and ablated. Agrees.

Findings:
- S1, should-fix. Two follow-ups have no carrier (`carrier: none · noted, not filed`). `tool.zod.ts` line 98 defines the confirmation's enforced set as "the doors that enforce the author's `ai.exposed` opt-in" and says REST `/actions` is not `ai.exposed`-gated; after this PR the REST route does read the opt-in for one pair, so the published reason is wrong for that pair. `flows.mdx` line 77 lists the start doors and their refusal with no account row, and the PR is BREAKING. The seat files a spec-lane card and a docs card before landing, so neither is lost.
- S2, should-fix, follow-up decision. The 403 sends the account to "the REST actions route or the MCP `run_action` tool" as equals, yet an author's `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` on that same action is asked on only one of them. Not owed by ruling C and not a defect of this diff; it needs its own decision card (the dev's question 2, option B).
- N1, nit. `flow.runAs === 'system'` is now spelled three times in `flow-start-admission.ts` (`isElevatedSelfTriggered`, `flowRunsElevated`, rule 2).
- N2, nit. ADR D3 says an agent principal "never runs `isSystem`", and an admitted run's facts now carry `isSystem: true` beside `principalKind: 'agent'`. The new Non-goals sentence is where a reader reconciles the two; D3 alone does not say so.

No must-fix.
